fields.notes: Security requirements at the Part 1 Architecture level cover the cryptographic and protocol semantics that the TPM must enforce — hierarchies + authorization + algorithm agility + protected storage + attestation + side-channel hardening obligation. Physical-tamper, EAL / CC, and FIPS-140 evaluation are delegated to the TCG TPM Protection Profile and to vendor security certifications.
fields.security_summary: The TPM 2.0 architecture provides four primitives that together form a hardware root of trust: (1) Root of Trust for Storage (RTS) — sealed data under PCR/policy and Storage hierarchy; (2) Root of Trust for Reporting (RTR) — PCR + TPM2_Quote signature under Endorsement hierarchy; (3) Root of Trust for Measurement (RTM) — initialized by host CPU / firmware then extended into PCRs; (4) algorithm-agile cryptographic library — supports RSA, ECC (NIST + SM2 + BN), SHA-1/256/384/512, SM3-256, AES (CFB/CBC/OFB/CTR/ECB), Camellia, SM4, TDES, HMAC.

security_features.name: Four hierarchies
security_features.description: Platform / Storage / Endorsement / Null — each rooted in its own Primary Seed; cross-hierarchy key derivation is forbidden.

security_features.name: Primary seeds (PPS/SPS/EPS)
security_features.description: ≥ 32-octet seeds; EPS is OTP from manufacture; SPS / PPS can be re-rolled under hierarchy authorization.

security_features.name: PCR (Platform Configuration Registers)
security_features.description: ≥ 24 PCRs per active hash bank; extend-only; PCR_new = H(PCR_old || measurement).

security_features.name: Multiple PCR banks
security_features.description: Simultaneous PCR banks per active hash algorithm — supports SHA-1, SHA-256, SHA-384, SHA-512, SM3-256.

security_features.name: Authorization sessions
security_features.description: Password, HMAC, Policy; HMAC binds across multiple commands; Policy evaluates rich authorization expressions.

security_features.name: Policy primitives
security_features.description: PolicyPCR, PolicySigned, PolicyAuthorize, PolicyOR, PolicyAuthValue, PolicyPassword, PolicyCounterTimer, PolicyCommandCode, PolicyLocality, PolicyNV, PolicyNvWritten.

security_features.name: Sealed data
security_features.description: TPM2_Create with type = TPM_ALG_KEYEDHASH + authPolicy = PolicyPCR seals secret to PCR state.

security_features.name: Attestation
security_features.description: TPM2_Quote signs PCR digest + qualifyingData under restricted Endorsement-hierarchy key.

security_features.name: Restricted keys
security_features.description: Restricted signing keys only sign TPM-internally-produced digests; restricted decryption keys only handle TPM-internal structures (Storage role).

security_features.name: Encrypted duplication
security_features.description: TPM2_Duplicate with TPMA_OBJECT.encryptedDuplication wraps the sensitive area under a parent-public encryption + symmetric inner wrap.

security_features.name: Dictionary-attack lockout
security_features.description: Configurable failure-count + recovery-time + lockout-recovery limits brute-force attacks.

security_features.name: Localities
security_features.description: 5 localities (0..4) — locality 4 reserved for the host CPU TEE; objects may be bound to locality via policy.

security_features.name: H-CRTM event sequence
security_features.description: Hardware Core Root of Trust for Measurement; first measurement of the host CPU's secure firmware extends PCR0.

security_features.name: Audit
security_features.description: Session-based audit + command-code audit produce signed digests over the audited command/response stream.

security_features.name: Field upgrade
security_features.description: TPM2_FieldUpgradeStart with vendor-signed manifest — protects against rollback and unauthorized firmware.

security_features.name: Side-channel hardening
security_features.description: Implementations are required to harden against timing, power, EM, and fault-injection side channels (Protection Profile).

algorithm_set_optional: ECC NIST P-384, P-521, BN-P256 (ECDAA), SM2 P-256
SHA-1 (legacy, deprecated for new use), SHA-384, SHA-512, SM3-256
fields.comparison_to_sibling_tpm_1_2: TPM 1.2 used fixed RSA-2048 + SHA1; introduced AIK + DRTM + Locality + NV. TPM 2.0 generalizes everything: algorithm-agile (any hash + RSA / ECC), HMAC + Policy sessions replace OIAP/OSAP, multi-bank PCRs, EK certificate chain. TPM 1.2 software cannot drive TPM 2.0 hardware (and vice versa) at the wire-format level.
